punchline: People solved creative insight puzzles better at their off-peak time of day, when they were a little less focused.
thirty_sec: Daniel Pink points to a study of hundreds of millions of tweets: mood rises in the morning, dips in the afternoon and rises again in the evening, roughly reversed for night owls. The morning peak is great for focused, analytical work. But in another study, people solved insight puzzles better at their non-optimal time, when a looser focus let odd connections through. So the real question isn't when you're productive, but for what.
question: When in the day does your best idea usually show up?
